lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Solomon and the congregation go to the high place at Gibeon, where the LORD appears and tells him to ask; he asks for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people and, because he did not ask for riches, God gives him wisdom, knowledge, riches, wealth and honour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked for at Gibeon and what God gave him?
ev: Say what Solomon asked and what God added (1:10-12)
Describe Solomon's wealth in 1:14-17

nodes.d: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)

nodes.t: Solomon prepares to build the temple
nodes.d: Solomon determines to build a house for the LORD's name, numbers workmen, and asks Huram king of Tyre for timber and a skilled craftsman; Huram answers, blessing the LORD, and sends a cunning man and the timber.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon arranged workers and timber for the temple?
ev: Say what Solomon asked from Huram (2:7-9)
Say how Huram responded (2:11-16)

nodes.d: Solomon begins to build on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to David and on the threshing floor of Ornan, in his fourth year; the house is overlaid with gold, with two cherubim in the most holy place, a veil, and two pillars named Jachin and Boaz.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe where Solomon built the temple and what was inside?
ev: Say where the temple was built (3:1)
Say what stood in the most holy house (3:10-13)

nodes.d: Solomon makes the bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, ten lavers, golden lampstands and tables, and the courts; Huram makes the bronze pieces, and everything inside is of gold.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the temple furnishings Solomon made?
ev: Name some of the furnishings and what the sea was used for (4:2-6)
Say what the vessels in the temple were made of (4:7-22)

nodes.t: The ark is brought in and the glory fills the house
nodes.d: At the feast the priests bring the ark of the covenant into the most holy place; when the singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, saying he is good and his mercy endures for ever, a cloud fills the house and the priests cannot minister because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was placed in the new temple?
ev: Say what was in the ark (5:10)
Describe what happened when the Levites praised the LORD (5:13-14)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the promise to David
nodes.d: Solomon says the LORD dwells in thick darkness, blesses the congregation, and says the LORD has performed his word to David: David's son has been set on the throne and built the house, in which the ark with the LORD's covenant is placed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Solomon says the LORD had promised David?
ev: Say what Solomon says the LORD promised David (6:5-9)
Say what Solomon says he has done (6:10-11)

nodes.d: Kneeling before the whole congregation, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be kept, and prays for the LORD to hear and forgive when Israel sins, is defeated, is in drought, or in captivity, and when a stranger prays toward the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple?
ev: Say what Solomon asks for if Israel repents (6:24-25, 36-39)
Find the request about the throne and David (6:16-17, 42)

nodes.t: Fire from heaven and the feast of dedication
nodes.d: When Solomon finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD fills the house; the people bow and praise, great sacrifices are offered, and they keep the dedication for seven days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Solomon prayed at the dedication?
ev: Describe what fell from heaven and how the people responded (7:1-3)
Say how many days they kept the feast (7:8-9)

nodes.d: The LORD appears to Solomon by night and says that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways he will hear, forgive and heal their land; he will establish Solomon's throne as he covenanted with David, but if they forsake him he will pluck them out of the land and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Solomon about humbling themselves and about forsaking him?
ev: State the condition and promise of 7:14
Say what the LORD warns will happen if they serve other gods (7:19-22)

nodes.d: Solomon builds cities, sets forced labour on the remaining peoples, keeps the burnt offerings and feasts as appointed, and orders the priests and Levites as David commanded; ships brought gold from Ophir.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon kept worship in order after the temple was built?
ev: Say how Solomon followed David's order for the priests and Levites (8:14-15)
Say what the ships brought (8:17-18)

nodes.t: The queen of Sheba and the end of Solomon's reign
nodes.d: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and blesses the LORD for setting him on the throne; the chapter describes his gold, throne, ships and wisdom, and ends with his forty-year reign and burial in the city of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and how Solomon's reign ended?
ev: Say what the queen said about the LORD (9:8)
State how long Solomon reigned (9:30)

nodes.d: At Shechem Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's yoke; he rejects the old men's counsel and answers roughly, and Israel rebels against the house of David, while Rehoboam reigns over the cities of Judah. The text says the cause was of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the northern tribes broke from Rehoboam?
ev: Compare what the old men and the young men advised (10:7-11)
Say what Israel said when the king answered roughly (10:16)

nodes.d: Rehoboam gathers an army to fight Israel but obeys the word of Shemaiah and returns; he fortifies cities, and priests and Levites and those who set their hearts to seek the LORD come to Judah from Jeroboam's kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Rehoboam did not go to war and why the priests and Levites came to Judah?
ev: Say why Rehoboam did not fight Israel (11:2-4)
Say why the Levites came to Judah (11:13-16)

nodes.d: When Rehoboam is strong he forsakes the law of the LORD, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt comes against Jerusalem; Shemaiah tells them the LORD has left them, and when they humble themselves the LORD grants some deliverance, though they become Shishak's servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Shishak came and how the LORD responded when Rehoboam humbled himself?
ev: Say what turned Judah to humility (12:5-7)
Say what Shishak took (12:9)

nodes.d: Abijah of Judah, standing on Mount Zemaraim, tells Jeroboam that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt, that Judah has not forsaken the LORD while Israel has made golden calves; Judah cries to the LORD and Israel is defeated.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Abijah said about David and why Judah won?
ev: Find the phrase about the covenant of salt (13:5)
Say why Judah prevailed (13:18)

nodes.t: Asa removes idols and defeats Zerah
nodes.d: Asa does good and right in the LORD's eyes, removes altars and high places, builds fenced cities during ten years of quiet, and when Zerah the Ethiopian comes with a huge host he cries to the LORD, saying it is nothing with him to help, and the LORD smites the Ethiopians.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Asa prayed and what happened to Zerah's army?
ev: Say what Asa prayed before the battle (14:11)
Say what Asa removed from Judah (14:3-5)

nodes.d: The Spirit of God comes on Azariah, who tells Asa that the LORD is with them while they are with him; Asa removes the idols, renews the altar, and Judah enters a covenant to seek the LORD with all their heart and soul, and he removes his mother Maachah from being queen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Azariah told Asa and what covenant Judah made?
ev: State Azariah's message (15:2)
Say what the covenant was and what it required (15:12-13)

nodes.t: Asa relies on Syria and not the LORD
nodes.d: In Asa's thirty-sixth year Baasha of Israel builds Ramah, and Asa takes treasures from the temple to hire Benhadad of Syria; Hanani the seer rebukes him for not relying on the LORD, and Asa imprisons him. In his illness he seeks physicians and not the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Asa's trust changed late in his reign?
ev: Say what Hanani told Asa (16:7-9)
Say how Asa responded to Hanani and in his disease (16:10, 12)

nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in the first ways of David and seeks the LORD, not Baalim; the LORD establishes his kingdom, and in the third year of his reign he sends princes, Levites and priests with the book of the law to teach through Judah's cities, so that fear of the LORD falls on the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Jehoshaphat taught Judah the law of the LORD?
ev: Say what Jehoshaphat sent teachers to do (17:7-9)
Say what the LORD did for Jehoshaphat (17:5, 10)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat joins Ahab and Micaiah warns
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and goes to Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying he will speak what God says, shows a lying spirit sent into the prophets' mouths. Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat cries out and God helps him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat went with Ahab and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare Micaiah with the four hundred prophets
Say how Ahab died and how Jehoshaphat was saved (18:30-34, 31)

nodes.d: Jehu the seer rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the ungodly yet notes the good in him; Jehoshaphat goes among the people turning them back to the LORD and sets judges in the fenced cities and in Jerusalem, telling them to judge for the LORD and fear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jehoshaphat set up judges and what he told them?
ev: Say what Jehoshaphat told the judges (19:6-7)
Say what Jehu the seer said was good in him (19:3)

nodes.t: The LORD fights for Judah against Moab and Ammon
nodes.d: A great multitude of Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir comes against Jehoshaphat, who proclaims a fast and prays that they have no might and their eyes are on God; Jahaziel says the battle is not theirs but God's, singers go before the army, and the LORD sets the enemy against each other.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Judah won the battle against Moab and Ammon without fighting?
ev: Quote the way Jahaziel describes the battle (20:15)
Describe how Judah went out to battle (20:20-22)

nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in Asa's way, though the high places remain; he joins Ahaziah of Israel to build ships at Ezion-geber and Eliezer prophesies that the LORD has broken his works, and the ships do not sail.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Jehoshaphat's ships were broken?
ev: Say what remained despite his good reign (20:33)
Say why the ships were broken (20:37)

nodes.d: Jehoram kills his brothers, walks as the house of Ahab did (for Ahab's daughter is his wife), yet the LORD does not destroy David's house because of his covenant with David. Elijah writes warning of plague and a disease of his bowels, and Jehoram dies of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God spared the house of David despite Jehoram?
ev: Say why the LORD did not destroy David's house (21:7)
Say what Elijah's writing announced (21:12-15)

nodes.t: Ahaziah, Athaliah and the hidden Joash
nodes.d: Ahaziah of Judah follows the counsel of Ahab's house and is killed with Joram of Israel by Jehu; Athaliah destroys the royal seed but Jehoshabeath hides the baby Joash in the house of God for six years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joash escaped Athaliah?
ev: Say who walked with Ahaziah and what happened to him (22:3-9)
Say who saved Joash and where he was hidden (22:11-12)

nodes.t: Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is slain
nodes.d: In the seventh year Jehoiada makes a covenant with the captains, brings out the king's son in the temple with guards and Levites, anoints him, and Athaliah is put to death; Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the people and the king, and the house of Baal is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Joash became king and how the people renewed their covenant?
ev: Say how Joash was crowned and who protected him (23:1-11)
State what the king's son reigning is said to fulfil (23:3)

nodes.t: Joash repairs the temple, then turns away
nodes.d: Joash repairs the house of the LORD with money collected in a chest, but after Jehoiada dies the princes lead him to serve idols; when Zechariah the priest warns them, Joash has him stoned in the temple court, and Joash is later struck down by Syrians and conspirators.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joash did well while Jehoiada lived and what changed after he died?
ev: Say how the temple was repaired (24:8-14)
Say what Joash did after Jehoiada's death (24:17-22)

nodes.d: Amaziah obeys the law about not killing children for fathers' sins, sends away hired Israelite troops at a prophet's word and defeats Edom, but then brings home Edom's gods and worships them. He ignores the prophet, challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth-shemesh, and is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Amaziah went from obeying the LORD to worshipping idols?
ev: Say what Amaziah did after defeating Edom (25:14)
Say why God was angry and what resulted (25:15-24)

nodes.d: Uzziah seeks God while Zechariah teaches him, and God makes him prosper with victories, buildings and an army; when he is strong his heart is lifted up, he enters the temple to burn incense, and the LORD strikes him with leprosy until his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Uzziah when he became strong?
ev: Say what led to Uzziah's success (26:5)
Say what he did to bring leprosy on himself (26:16-21)

nodes.d: Jotham does right as Uzziah did, but does not enter the temple; he builds in Jerusalem and Judah, conquers Ammon, and becomes mighty because he prepared his ways before the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what made Jotham a strong king?
ev: Say why Jotham became mighty (27:6)
Name something he built or won

nodes.d: Ahaz walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes images for Baalim and burns his children; the LORD delivers him to Syria and Israel, where Pekah kills many in Judah in one day. In his distress he sends to Assyria, who does not help, and he closes the temple and sets up altars everywhere.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Ahaz responded to his troubles and what happened?
ev: List what Ahaz did instead of seeking the LORD (28:2-4, 22-25)
Say what happened when he turned to Assyria (28:20-21)

nodes.t: Oded and the captives sent home
nodes.d: When Israel brings home 200,000 captives from Judah, the prophet Oded meets the army and says they also have sins and must send them back; some Ephraimite leaders agree, and clothe, feed and carry the captives to Jericho.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israelites showed kindness to the captives from Judah?
ev: Say what Oded told the army (28:9-11)
Describe how the leaders cared for the captives (28:15)

nodes.t: Hezekiah cleanses and reopens the temple
nodes.d: Hezekiah reopens the doors of the LORD's house in his first year, calls the priests and Levites to sanctify it and carry out the filth, and says he intends to make a covenant with the LORD; sin offerings are made for the kingdom and the sanctuary, and worship with singing and instruments resumes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah restored worship in the temple?
ev: Say what Hezekiah told the Levites (29:5-11)
Describe how worship was restored (29:25-30)

nodes.d: Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, including Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, in the second month; some mock but many humble themselves and come, and the people keep the feast with great joy for fourteen days. Hezekiah prays for those who were not cleansed and the LORD heals the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Hezekiah invited all Israel to the Passover and how the people responded?
ev: Say whom Hezekiah invited (30:1-9)
Say what Hezekiah prayed for the uncleansed (30:18-20)

nodes.t: Hezekiah organises the offerings and priests
nodes.d: After the Passover Israel breaks down the idols, Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses, and the people bring tithes and firstfruits in abundance; storerooms are prepared and men are appointed to distribute. The text says Hezekiah did this with all his heart and prospered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Hezekiah arranged for the support of the priests and Levites?
ev: Say what the people brought (31:5-6)
Say how Hezekiah served God according to 31:20-21

nodes.t: Sennacherib threatens and the LORD delivers Jerusalem
nodes.d: Sennacherib invades Judah; Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem and tells the people there is more with them than with the king of Assyria. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and the LORD sends an angel to cut off the Assyrian leaders; Sennacherib goes home and his sons kill him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, and what God did?
ev: Say what Hezekiah told the people (32:7-8)
Say what the LORD did after Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed (32:20-22)

nodes.d: Hezekiah is sick to death and prays and is given a sign, but his heart is lifted up and wrath falls on Judah until he and Jerusalem humble themselves. He prospers, stops the upper watercourse of Gihon, and when envoys come from Babylon God leaves him to test what was in his heart; he dies and is honoured in burial.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah's heart was tested and what the LORD did?
ev: Say what happened because of Hezekiah's pride and how it was turned aside (32:25-26)
Name something Hezekiah built for Jerusalem (32:30)

nodes.d: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sets idols in the house of God; the LORD brings Assyria's captains, who take him in fetters to Babylon, and there he humbles himself, prays and is restored to Jerusalem, where he removes the idols and repairs the altar. His son Amon does evil and does not humble himself, and is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Manasseh turned back to the LORD and how Amon was different?
ev: Say what happened to Manasseh in affliction and what he did after returning (33:11-16)
Say how Amon differed from his father (33:23)

nodes.t: Josiah seeks God and purges the land
nodes.d: Josiah begins to seek the God of David in his eighth year, and in his twelfth year purges Judah and Jerusalem of high places, groves and images, and also in Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon and Naphtali; in his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan and others to repair the house of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Josiah did in the early years of his reign?
ev: Say when Josiah began to seek God and when he began to purge (34:3)
Say who oversaw the temple repair (34:8-13)

nodes.t: The book of the law found and the covenant renewed
nodes.d: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah tears his clothes, sends to Huldah the prophetess, who says the evil will come but not in his days because he humbled himself. Josiah reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to keep his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the book of the law was found and what Josiah did next?
ev: Say what Josiah did when the book was read (34:19)
Say what Huldah told him and what covenant he made (34:23-31)

nodes.d: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the fourteenth of the first month, appointing priests and Levites to their duties, giving offerings to the people, with the singers in their places as David commanded; no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since Samuel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Josiah's Passover and what made it special?
ev: Say how Josiah organised the Levites and priests (35:2-6)
Say how this Passover compared to earlier ones (35:18)

nodes.d: Pharaoh Necho goes up to fight at Carchemish and warns Josiah not to meddle, saying God commanded him; Josiah does not heed and goes out to fight at Megiddo, where archers wound him, and he dies; all Judah mourns, and Jeremiah laments for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Josiah died and who mourned for him?
ev: Say what Necho told Josiah (35:21)
Say what Josiah did and what happened (35:22-24)

nodes.d: Jehoahaz is deposed by the king of Egypt, Jehoiakim is bound by Nebuchadnezzar and temple vessels are taken to Babylon; Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon, and Zedekiah rebels, hardens his heart, and with the priests and people pollutes the house of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Judah's last kings in order and say what happened to each?
ev: Say what Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylon (36:7, 10)
Say how Zedekiah and the people sinned (36:12-14)

nodes.t: The LORD sends Judah into exile
nodes.d: The LORD sent messengers to his people because of his compassion, but they mocked the prophets until there was no remedy; the Chaldeans burn the house of God, break down Jerusalem's wall, and carry the survivors to Babylon until the land enjoyed its sabbaths, seventy years, as Jeremiah spoke.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Judah went into exile according to 2 Chronicles 36?
ev: Say why the LORD sent the messengers and how they were treated (36:15-16)
Say what the seventy years were to fulfil (36:21)

nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the LORD stirs up his spirit to proclaim that the LORD God of heaven has charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and invites any of his people to go up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how 2 Chronicles closes and what Cyrus announced?
ev: Say whose spirit the LORD stirred up and what he proclaimed
Say how 2 Chronicles ends

nodes.d: Standing before the altar, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be confirmed, and prays that God will hear and forgive in specific situations of sin, defeat, famine, a stranger's prayer and exile.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's dedication prayer and what he asks for?
ev: Say what Solomon asks God to do when his people sin and then repent (8:33-34, 46-50)
Find where Solomon asks God to keep his word to David (8:25-26)

nodes.t: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time
nodes.d: The LORD says he has hallowed the house and promises to establish Solomon's throne for ever as he promised David if Solomon walks in integrity, but warns that if Israel and their children turn away he will cut Israel off and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the conditions the LORD set before Solomon after the temple was finished?
ev: State the promise and the warning (9:4-7)
Say what the nations would conclude if Israel forsook the LORD (9:8-9)

nodes.d: Rehoboam rejects the old men's counsel and answers Israel harshly; ten tribes break away and make Jeroboam king while Judah stays with Rehoboam. The text says the cause was from the LORD, and Shemaiah forbids war against their brethren.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the kingdom of Israel was divided after Solomon?
ev: Compare the counsel of the old men and the young men (12:7, 10-11)
Say which tribes followed Rehoboam and which followed Jeroboam

nodes.d: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying the LORD's word, describes Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths. Ahab puts Micaiah in prison.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat wanted to hear a prophet of the LORD and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare the four hundred prophets and Micaiah
Say what Ahab did with Micaiah (22:26-27)

nodes.t: Athaliah and the hidden king Joash
nodes.d: After Ahaziah's death Athaliah destroys the royal seed and reigns six years; Jehosheba hides the baby Joash in the house of the LORD, and in the seventh year Jehoiada anoints him, Athaliah is put to death, and Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how young Joash became king of Judah?
ev: Say how Joash was saved and for how long he was hidden
Say what the covenant of Jehoiada was (11:17)

nodes.d: Amaziah does right, though not like David, kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children as the law of Moses says, defeats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh, with Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple treasures taken. He is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Amaziah's reign, including his pride in challenging Israel?
ev: Say what Amaziah did and did not do with the children of the murderers (14:5-6)
Describe the result of his challenge to Israel (14:11-14)

nodes.d: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays; Isaiah says the LORD will defend the city for his own sake and David's sake, and that night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God answered Hezekiah's prayer against Sennacherib?
ev: Retell Hezekiah's prayer and what he asked (19:15-19)
Say what happened to the Assyrian army (19:35)

nodes.t: Josiah and the book of the law
nodes.d: In Josiah's eighteenth year, repairs to the temple turn up the book of the law; the king tears his clothes at its words, and Huldah the prophetess says the evil will come on Jerusalem but not in Josiah's days because his heart was tender.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the book of the law was found in the temple?
ev: Say what Hilkiah found and how Josiah reacted (22:8-11)
Say what Huldah told Josiah (22:16-20)

nodes.t: Josiah's death and Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
nodes.d: Josiah dies at Megiddo when Pharaoh-nechoh goes up to Assyria; Jehoahaz reigns three months and is taken to Egypt, and Pharaoh makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim, who taxes the land to pay him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Judah's kings right after Josiah?
ev: Say how Josiah died (23:29-30)
Say who appointed Jehoiakim (23:34)

nodes.d: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?
ev: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)

nodes.d: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?
ev: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)

nodes.t: Cyrus's decree and the first return
nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus the LORD stirs his spirit, and he proclaims that the LORD God of heaven charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites any of God's people to go up. Those whose spirit God raised go, neighbours help them, and Cyrus brings out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Cyrus decreed and who went up to Jerusalem?
ev: Say whose word was being fulfilled (1:1)
Say what Cyrus returned to Sheshbazzar (1:7-11)
